account: So far today the town appears to be following its ordinary routines. During my market walk I heard that the baker had carried wheat at the bakery and later a sack of bread across the bridge. I have now seen the baker carrying bread and putting it into the bakery stall chest at about eleven, which fits the neighbour's report that fresh bread would reach the market. The neighbour mentioned talk of supposed bakery decorations, but said they had asked the baker directly and learned that these were only oven glow. I have not seen any decorations myself, and I have no firm evidence of a special gathering or secret undertaking. The builder is walking through town carrying a lantern; I do not know its intended use. My afternoon tea is confirmed with the neighbour at three at the east-bank cottage at (16, -60, 105). The secretary had gone to verify the host and address because the appointment book was vague. For now, bread production and market restocking explain the clearest activity I have observed; anything beyond that remains uncertain.
